cards.headline: Technician killed after vehicle falls off lift at Stuart auto shop
cards.teaser: A technician died Wednesday morning at an auto shop in Stuart after a vehicle fell off a lift.
cards.body:
A technician died Wednesday morning at an auto shop in Stuart after a vehicle fell off a lift. The incident occurred at a Stuart auto repair facility, according to reports.

Details about the specific location of the auto shop and the identity of the victim were not provided in initial reports. The incident happened Wednesday morning.

The circumstances surrounding how the vehicle fell from the lift remain under investigation. Auto lift accidents are rare but can be fatal when safety protocols are not followed or equipment malfunctions.

Authorities are investigating the workplace death. No information was available about whether other workers were present or injured during the incident.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man, 78, arrested for pointing loaded gun at pregnant driver during road rage incident
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested Robert Kniceley, 78, on Tuesday afternoon after he allegedly pointed a loaded handgun at a pregnant driver during a road rage incident. Kniceley was driving a yellow Chevrolet pickup truck east on St. Lucie West Boulevard when he began honking and driving aggressively near the victim's vehicle. He pulled up alongside her at the intersection of SW Peacock Boulevard and SW St. Lucie West Boulevard, and when she rolled down her window, he allegedly pointed a handgun at her.

The victim is in the late stages of pregnancy and became scared for her safety, according to police. She provided video evidence of the man leaving the area, which allowed police to track Kniceley's license plate to his residence. At his home, officers recovered a loaded Smith & Wesson .22 caliber handgun with a round in the chamber. Kniceley was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and transported to St. Lucie County Jail. A risk protection order seizure process was initiated as part of the investigation.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds defends Florida immigration detention costs, seeks federal reimbursement
cards.teaser: Byron Donalds, the Republican front-runner for Florida governor, defended the state's costly immigration enforcement expansion on Tuesday after officially quali.
cards.body:
Byron Donalds, the Republican front-runner for Florida governor, officially qualified for his gubernatorial bid on Tuesday with President Donald Trump's endorsement and U.S. Senator Rick Scott's support. When asked about Florida's costly expansion of immigration enforcement, including the Everglades detention center known as "Alligator Alcatraz," Donalds called it "mission accomplished" despite the state spending hundreds of millions of dollars on construction and operations. He argued that Florida stepped in when the federal government lacked sufficient detention resources and said the state should be reimbursed as responsibility shifts back to Washington. The federal government has already sent Florida an initial reimbursement of about $58 million. When asked whether he would push to recover the remaining costs, Donalds said: "Of course. We're going to work very hard to make that happen."

On property taxes, Donalds supports the proposed constitutional amendment on the November ballot that would increase the homestead exemption on non-school property taxes from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. The measure requires at least 60 percent voter approval. He acknowledged that lawmakers and the next governor would have to confront difficult questions about lost local revenue and the cost of essential services, including law enforcement, transportation and infrastructure. On artificial intelligence regulation, Donalds broke with Trump's push for a unified national framework, saying state-level regulation is the way to go because it is hard to move anything through Washington.

cards.headline: England's World Cup team trains in Palm Beach Gardens after 1-0 win over New Zealand
cards.body:
England's national soccer team won a pre-World Cup friendly match against New Zealand 1-0 in Tampa over the weekend, with Harry Kane scoring on a header. The team is now preparing at facilities in Palm Beach Gardens before relocating to its Kansas City base camp this weekend. England has scheduled another warm-up match in Orlando before the World Cup tournament officially begins.

Manager Thomas Tuchel outlined his expectations for the team's training in Palm Beach Gardens, emphasizing the importance of building intensity and improving their style of play. "We expect to push tomorrow physically and from intensity and style of play, ball speed and everything. We want to take the next step," Tuchel said. He also highlighted the quality of the facilities available to the team in the area. Defender Marc Guehi shared similar praise for both the accommodations and training venue, noting the welcoming atmosphere the team has experienced. "Great, fantastic. Everyone is super friendly and welcoming to us, felt at home straight away here, and in West Palm Beach. The quality of the pitch, really good so far," Guehi said.

Adjusting to Florida's climate has been a significant challenge for the squad. Guehi acknowledged that the first day of training in the summer heat was extremely difficult but that the team is gradually adapting to the conditions. "First day was extremely hot. We've been doing better getting used to the weather, getting used to the conditions, definitely a big step for us," Guehi said. At Gardens District Park, groundskeeping staff waters the fields moments before practice sessions begin. According to Palm Beach Gardens Director of Agronomy Andrew Keller, this preparation serves an important purpose. The moisture on the grass helps the ball move quickly across the surface rather than catching and slowing down, allowing players to replicate the playing conditions they will encounter in actual World Cup stadiums, where similar watering practices occur before matches.

England will depart South Florida this weekend for Kansas City, where the team will be based during the tournament. The squad's first World Cup match is scheduled for next Wednesday against Croatia. After England leaves, World Cup preparations will continue at the same Palm Beach Gardens facilities, as Portugal's national team is also planning to train on the fields.

cards.headline: David Jolly selects Gwen Graham as running mate in Florida governor's race
cards.body:
Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly announced Wednesday at the state Capitol that former Congresswoman Gwen Graham will be his running mate for the 2026 election. Graham, whose father was late Florida Governor and U.S. Senator Bob Graham, brings a recognized name to the ticket. Jolly has positioned his campaign as a bipartisan effort to attract Democrats, independents, and Republicans who are unhappy with the current state government's direction.

Jolly, a former Republican congressman who previously served alongside Graham in Congress, emphasized that her background and experience were the primary reasons for selecting her rather than strategic political considerations. "I had one goal in this process: to identify a governing partner capable of leading this state, not just as lieutenant governor, but as governor," Jolly said. Graham outlined the ticket's priorities as affordability, education, health care, and insurance costs. She stressed that both candidates want to move beyond what she called divisive cultural battles and address an economy that does not work for everyone alongside problems in the education system.

However, the selection may face resistance within Democratic circles. Graham has long been associated with the party's establishment wing, and her potential involvement in the campaign had previously disappointed some progressives who sought greater diversity in the party's statewide candidates. Jolly responded to these concerns by asserting that the campaign remains committed to addressing disparities that affect communities of color. He further contended that Republican frontrunner Byron Donalds has failed to adequately address these issues. The Donalds campaign responded swiftly to the announcement, characterizing Jolly and Graham as failed politicians with a failed liberal agenda.

The announcement occurs amid ongoing conflict within the Republican primary. Former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lieutenant Jay Collins, and James Fishback have all requested a debate before the August primary. Donalds has countered that his Republican opponents are polling too low to warrant a debate and has called for Republican unity heading into the November general election. The dynamics of both races continue to develop as candidates prepare for the campaign season ahead.

hero.headline: Portugal's national soccer team arrives at North County District Park for World Cup training in Palm Beach Gardens
hero.teaser: Portugal's national team is preparing to train at North County District Park in Palm Beach Gardens ahead of the World Cup, which kicks off tomorrow.
hero.body:
Portugal's national soccer team is preparing to settle into North County District Park in Palm Beach Gardens as the World Cup gets underway. On Wednesday, journalists covering the Portuguese team gathered at the facility for a briefing session with media liaisons ahead of the squad's official arrival. The session was designed to set expectations and coordinate logistics between the team and the press corps.

Marco Carvalho, the media coordinator who has held his position for three decades, led the debriefing and expressed his satisfaction with the Palm Beach Gardens location. "We have to work with the media, with all the media to have a great World Cup," Carvalho said. He emphasized that his goal is to ensure a smooth experience for everyone involved in covering the team. When asked about the facilities, Carvalho offered enthusiastic praise. "In World Cup, in Europeans, I think it's a good spot, a very good spot," he said, drawing on his extensive experience with international tournaments.

Tim Ford, the sports and special facilities director, is overseeing preparations for Portugal's temporary training home. Ford noted that the facility is receiving final touches before the team's arrival. Portugal will use training fields adjacent to those currently occupied by England's national team, which has been training at the complex for the past week. Ford explained that hosting England first provided valuable learning opportunities for the city. "Each one we host, we get to know the intricacies of what each team is looking for and each time it seems we tightened down and dial in more," Ford said. "We feel really good but at the same time we try not to get complacent."

Security measures at the facility will be significantly enhanced following Portugal's arrival. Journalists were granted access to view the team's training center in the back portion of the complex, but Portugal requested that any video footage remain unpublished until Saturday to allow the team to experience its first practice without prior exposure. This arrangement underscores the level of coordination between local officials and the national team to ensure optimal preparation conditions as the World Cup tournament begins.

The victim, who is in the late stages of pregnancy, became scared for her safety. She provided video evidence of the man leaving the area.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach man faces multiple charges after dragging FHP trooper during traffic stop in Boynton Beach
cards.teaser: A 34-year-old Riviera Beach man was arrested Sunday after a Florida Highway Patrol trooper was dragged following a traffic stop at the Interstate 95 exit ramp in Boynton Beach.
cards.body:
A Riviera Beach man faces multiple charges after a Florida Highway Patrol trooper was dragged during a traffic stop in Boynton Beach on Sunday. The incident began at 3:41 p.m. when a trooper spotted a beige Honda Accord with an expired tag on I-95 near the Boynton Beach Boulevard exit. The trooper pulled over the vehicle on the exit ramp, where the driver, Devontea Stubbs, 34, said his friend was the registered owner. Stubbs was unable to locate the registration and did not have a driver's license. The trooper learned that Stubbs had his license suspended 11 times since 2014, including two indefinite cancellations, and had a possible statewide extradition warrant for Palm Beach County in a burglary case.

When the trooper opened the driver's side door and reached into the vehicle after Stubbs refused to exit, Stubbs shifted the vehicle into drive. The trooper was still within the passenger compartment when the Honda rapidly accelerated, traveling about 15 feet before the trooper could exit. Stubbs continued southbound on I-95, ignoring red lights and colliding with a Toyota at the Boynton Beach Boulevard intersection. He then traveled west on Boynton Beach Boulevard at speeds exceeding 75 mph in a 35 mph zone and turned northbound onto Old Boynton Road at 80 mph in a 30 mph zone. Boynton Beach police arrested Stubbs with K-9 Ash at approximately 4:40 p.m. at the Sealofts at Boynton Village apartments. Stubbs faces charges including aggravated fleeing and eluding, aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer, resisting arrest, and driving with a suspended license.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach man accused of dragging FHP trooper during I-95 traffic stop in Boynton Beach
cards.teaser: A trooper was dragged about 15 feet after stopping a Honda Accord with an expired tag on the I-95 exit ramp at Boynton Beach Boulevard on Sunday. The driver faces multiple charges including aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer.
cards.body:
A Riviera Beach man faces multiple charges after a Florida Highway Patrol trooper was dragged during a traffic stop on an Interstate 95 exit ramp in Boynton Beach on Sunday, according to law enforcement. FHP said the incident started at 3:41 p.m. when a trooper on I-95 near the Boynton Beach Boulevard exit spotted a beige Honda Accord with an expired tag not assigned to any vehicle. The trooper pulled over the Accord on the exit ramp and stopped on the outside shoulder. Driver Devontea Stubbs, 34, told the trooper his friend was the registered owner and he was unaware of the expired tag. Stubbs was unable to locate the registration and did not have a driver's license. The trooper later learned that Stubbs had his license suspended 11 times since 2014, including two indefinite cancellations, along with a possible statewide extradition warrant for Palm Beach County in a burglary case.

When a second trooper arrived and asked Stubbs to step out of the vehicle, Stubbs remained seated questioning why they needed to discuss his license. When the trooper opened the driver's side door and reached into the vehicle, Stubbs rapidly shifted the Honda into drive. The trooper said the vehicle traveled about 15 feet before he could exit. Stubbs continued southbound, ignoring red lights and hitting a Toyota at the I-95 southbound exit ramp at Boynton Beach Boulevard. He then traveled west on Boynton Beach Boulevard at speeds over 75 mph in a 35 mph zone and entered opposing lanes to pass other motorists. Boynton Beach police arrested Stubbs with help from K-9 Ash at the Sealofts at Boynton Village apartments at about 4:40 p.m. Stubbs faces charges including aggravated fleeing and eluding with injury or damage, aggravated battery on a law enforcement officer, resisting arrest, driving while license suspended, burglary and petit theft.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Square mall redevelopment study draws mixed reactions from shoppers and business owners
hero.teaser: A 2023 Martin County study explored redevelopment options for Treasure Coast Square Mall, including apartments, an amphitheater, and outdoor green space. Shoppers and business owners have mixed feelings about potential changes to the decades-old community fixture.
hero.body:
Treasure Coast Square Mall has been a community landmark for many years, and discussions about its future have recently gained attention. In 2023, Martin County commissioned a study to explore potential redevelopment options for the property. The study examined possibilities including residential apartments, an amphitheater, and green space designed in an outdoor format. County officials have characterized the effort as a planning exercise rather than a commitment to change.

Shoppers express a range of opinions about the mall's current state and potential improvements. Liz Permar said "It's always been a fun place to go to" and believes a facelift would be beneficial. Kimberly Grucza appreciates the concept of an update but has reservations about one specific aspect of the proposal. She stated "I like the idea of an update," but expressed concern about the apartment component, noting that "we already have so many" residential options in the area. While shoppers generally welcome improvements, not everyone supports every element of the proposed redevelopment.

Business owners operating inside the mall are closely monitoring the redevelopment discussion because any changes could directly affect their operations. Jessica Henry, who owns Plantitude and Flame, emphasized her hope that "if it goes through, you know they do more open concept stores where we're still able to have our business." Ron Gustafson, owner of MVP Sport Cards, reports that his store has thrived at its current location. He stated "The model of the mall store has worked for us. The store has been tremendously successful." However, Gustafson also identified maintenance issues that concern him. He noted experiencing water leaks in his store and believes the facility requires attention. According to Gustafson, "I think it's in neglect. I think with some effort and the right management this could turn around."

The status of the redevelopment proposal remains uncertain. Martin County Administrator Don Donaldson confirmed that what began as a planning study continues to be exactly that, with no firm decisions made about moving forward. Both the mall management and county officials have characterized the study as exploratory in nature, leaving the future direction of Treasure Coast Square Mall open to question. Whether the property will undergo significant changes or remain largely as it is will depend on decisions yet to be made by county leadership and other stakeholders.

PEBB Enterprises and Banyan Development have completed the sale of the Lowe's building at Shoppes at Southern Grove in Port St. Lucie's Tradition community. The transaction marks a commercial real estate deal in the growing Tradition area.

The Shoppes at Southern Grove is a retail center located within the Tradition community in Port St. Lucie. The center serves residents in St. Lucie County with shopping and services.

PEBB Enterprises and Banyan Development partnered on the sale of the individual building that houses Lowe's. The sale was completed on Tuesday.

The buyer and purchase price were not disclosed in the announcement. The Lowe's store continues to operate at the location following the ownership change.

cards.body: West Palm Beach's first Trader Joe's location will open at 9 a.m. on June 12 at 8111 South Dixie Highway, at the intersection of South Dixie Highway and Gregory Road. The 9,404-square-foot store will feature a grand opening celebration and giveaways. WPTV confirmed in August 2025 that the store was coming to West Palm Beach before the exact location was disclosed. Residents said they were excited for a store closer to them, with many previously having to drive to Wellington, Palm Beach Gardens or Delray Beach to shop at Trader Joe's.

cards.headline: Boca Raton studies impact of Florida property tax reform on city budget
cards.teaser: City leaders in Boca Raton were briefed Tuesday on the potential impact of property tax reform in Florida. Revenues for the city would drop $8.14 million in the first year and $16.7 million in the second year under a referendum before voters this November.
cards.body:
City leaders in Boca Raton were briefed on the potential impact of property tax reform in Florida during a council workshop on Tuesday. Deputy City Manager James Zervis presented data showing that two randomly selected homes in the city would likely see property tax reductions of around $2,000 per year. However, the city's revenues would drop $8.14 million in the first year and $16.7 million in the second year as a result of the reform.

The referendum before voters this November would raise the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Zervis told the council that policy direction would be needed to address the lost revenue, which could involve exploring other sources of revenue such as higher fees and additional taxes, cuts in services, and raising the millage rate on property taxes. Mayor Andy Thompson acknowledged the projected shortfall in the city's $250 million budget is significant but said it can be manageable for Boca Raton. Thompson stated that the city will likely take a mixed approach rather than relying on a single mechanism to address the revenue loss.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County braces for largest department budget cuts in history due to potential property tax cuts
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County officials are bracing for what could be the largest budget cuts in the county's history, as proposed property tax reductions threaten to eliminate nearly $400 million from county operations over the next two years.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County officials are bracing for what could be the largest budget cuts in the county's history, as proposed property tax reductions threaten to eliminate nearly $400 million from county operations over the next two years. County Administrator Joe Abruzzo announced during a budget meeting that if the property tax reduction passes, the county's budget for 30 departments could drop from $609 million to approximately $210 million, a loss of more than 65% of current funding. The Palm Beach County Fire Department alone stands to lose just under $200 million in funding under the proposed tax structure. The cuts would affect virtually every county service, including parks, libraries, roads and other essential operations. A major concern raised during the meeting centers on the proposed $250,000 homestead exemption, which may not represent the final figure. Abruzzo warned commissioners that the exemption could potentially increase to $500,000, further deepening the budget shortfall.

To help offset the budget shortfall, county officials discussed various revenue-generating options, including charging for parking at county beaches. Commissioners agreed they do not want residents to pay too much to park but reached an agreement on implementing beach parking fees as one measure to help bridge the funding gap. County leaders are also examining millage rates and identifying cost-saving opportunities, with particular attention on the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office budget, which has increased more than 216% over the past 20 years. Mike Caruso, the Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller, suggested increasing the limit on how much the county is allowed to invest in Israel bonds from 15% to 20%, which would earn the county an additional $3 million a year in interest income. Commissioners agreed the maximum millage rate will be set in July, with the complete budget scheduled for approval in September.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Council approves new rules for President Trump's Mar-a-Lago helipad
cards.teaser: Council members in Palm Beach met Tuesday to approve new rules for governing the use of a helipad at President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago club. The helipad was approved in October and will measure 60 feet in diameter and sit on the west lawn.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Town Council unanimously approved a revised fifth amendment to helipad rules at President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago club in a 5-0 vote. The new regulations specify that during Trump's second term, the helipad shall be used exclusively for transporting Trump for business related to the presidency only. The 60-foot-diameter helipad will sit on the west lawn, the same location as during Trump's first term.

Once Trump's second term ends, the helipad shall be used exclusively by government aircraft for emergency use by Trump or Melania Trump, as determined by the U.S. Secret Service and provided Secret Service personnel are onboard. In emergencies, the helipad may also be used by federal, state or local law enforcement, fire-rescue, emergency medical service, or other first responder agencies. All other use is strictly prohibited, including by Mar-a-Lago members, guests, private parties, other protectees, or Trump family members who are not protectees. Violations will result in a $15,000 fine payable to the Town of Palm Beach within 10 days. Each subsequent violation will increase the fine by $10,000. Construction of the helipad is scheduled for this summer while the club is closed for the season.

cards.headline: Boca Raton families raise concerns over homelessness in city parks
cards.teaser: Boca Raton's mayor is taking steps to address a growing homelessness problem in city parks, as families raise safety concerns about the issue. New no trespassing signs are appearing at parks across the city, including Wildflower Park near the Intracoastal Waterway.
cards.body:
Boca Raton families are expressing concerns about homelessness in city parks as the problem grows more visible. Elina Gundersen, a parent who visits Wildflower Park regularly with her four children, said the presence of homeless individuals has created discomfort. "It doesn't feel very comfortable having some of that homeless population in the areas where children would typically be hanging out," Gundersen said, noting that homeless individuals spend time by picnic tables and occupy bathrooms. She said the problem appears to be worsening and called for patrolling or additional help.

Mayor Andy Thomson acknowledged the issue is a growing concern in areas including Sanborn Square, Wildflower Park and Silver Palm Park. In February, the city passed an ordinance to add trespassing signage at parks, making clear that parks are not places for people to set up temporary homes. Thomson said park rangers are being trained to work more closely with police to address the issue. The city is also working with Boca Helping Hands, a nonprofit operating since 1998 that feeds 160 people six times a week and connects individuals with housing and job opportunities. CEO Andrew Hagen said the organization aims to help people get back on their feet.

England will depart South Florida this weekend for Kansas City, where the team will be based during the tournament. The squad's first World Cup match is scheduled for next Wednesday against Croatia. After England leaves, World Cup preparations will continue at the same Palm Beach Gardens facilities, as Portugal's national team is also planning to train on the fields.

cards.headline: Portugal's national soccer team arrives at Palm Beach Gardens for World Cup training
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Gardens is welcoming its second soccer powerhouse ahead of the World Cup, which kicks off tomorrow. Media members covering Portugal's national team arrived at North County District Park on Wednesday for a debriefing ahead of the team's arrival.
cards.body:
On Wednesday, media members covering Portugal's national team arrived at North County District Park for a briefing ahead of the team's arrival in Palm Beach Gardens. Media coordinator Marco Carvalho, who has held his position for three decades, led the session for intermediaries between the team and press. "We have to work with the media, with all the media to have a great World Cup," Carvalho said. He expressed confidence in the Palm Beach Gardens facility, calling it "a very good spot" for World Cup preparation.

Tim Ford, sports and special facilities director, is overseeing construction of the team's temporary home. Portugal will train on fields adjacent to those used by England over the past week. Ford said hosting England first provided valuable preparation. "Each one we host, we get to know the intricacies of what each team is looking for and each time it seems we tightened down and dial in more," Ford said. Security around the facility will be heightened upon the team's arrival. Portugal requested that video of the training center not be published until Saturday, allowing the team to view the space during its first practice.

cards.headline: Six-time Grammy winner BeBe Winans to perform at Kravis Center in West Palm Beach on Saturday
cards.teaser: Gospel singer BeBe Winans will perform at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach this weekend. The six-time Grammy Award winner said he hopes his singing will be inspirational.
cards.body:
Six-time Grammy Award winner BeBe Winans will perform at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach this weekend as part of a Gospel Gala. During a recent interview, Winans discussed his hopes for the performance, emphasizing the inspirational impact he aims to have on attendees. "Everyone who is coming to the concert, we all are facing our own battles, but when you leave the concert, what I pray is that you have answers for those battles. You have another way of thinking towards those battles," Winans said.

Winans comes from a family of musical talent. His sister, CeCe Winans, has won 18 Grammy awards. The performance will take place Saturday, June 13, at the Kravis Center at 7 p.m.

hero.headline: Delray Beach Public Library launches free summer STREAM programs for kids and teens
hero.body:
The Delray Beach Public Library is brightening summer for young people with free STREAM programs covering Science, Technology, Reading, Art, Engineering, and Math. All Florida residents are welcome to participate in the initiatives held at the library's 36,000-square-foot downtown facility located at Atlantic Avenue and Swinton Avenue. The building draws more than 193,000 visitors annually and has served the community since 1913, when 30 women from the Ladies Improvement Society each contributed a book to launch the collection.

Young adult librarian Natalie Baron is directing teen programs including ColorSpace: Artistic Excavations, which allows teens to explore art history spanning from cave paintings to ancient pottery. Participants can also engage in lab-based activities such as collaborative 3D puzzle builds and select themed book boxes. Meanwhile, Mandy Fulop, head of the children's department, is launching the STREAM Into Summer Literacy Program. This initiative encourages young readers to establish reading goals with librarians, track their progress, and receive an Unearth a Story bag containing a free STREAM book and related activities.

In collaboration with the School District of Palm Beach County, the library provides free lunch daily from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., along with snacks from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m., for youth up to age 18. Family Nights held on select Tuesdays welcome children ages 5 and older to explore STREAM topics together. Saturday Science Discovery programs for ages 9 to 12 feature hands-on archaeology experiences including activities called Piece Together History, trash bag archaeology, carbon dating activities, and fossil hunts.

The library will host special guest speakers on select Thursdays throughout the summer. Malachi Fenn from the Florida Public Archaeology Network visits June 11, followed by Sea Turtle Adventures beach cleanup on June 25, American Shark Conservancy's SharkSmarts program on July 2, and FPAN Beyond Artifacts on July 16. According to Kae Jonsons, director of development and community relations, these free, high-quality programs help address summer learning gaps while keeping families engaged in accessible, safe community spaces. Registration for all programs is available at delraylibrary.org, where visitors can find the complete program lineup and event details.

cards.headline: Cornell Art Museum in Delray Beach opens upcycled art exhibit running through September
cards.teaser: The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square has opened Persistence of Matter, an exhibition spotlighting artists who turn discarded materials into sculptures, installations, and mixed media pieces.
cards.body:
The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square has opened its newest summer exhibition, Persistence of Matter, spotlighting artists who turn discarded materials into striking works of art. According to Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority Cultural Arts Director Marusca Gatto, the show underscores the museum's mission to marry creativity with community impact. Guest curators Mavis Benson and Pamela Lambie have selected artists whose sculptures, installations, and mixed media pieces are all crafted from reclaimed objects. Featured creators include Autumn Kioti, whose work draws on natural and urban influences, and Mike Silverman, whose Self-Reflection series uses discarded hard drive platters and printed circuit boards to create reflective sculptures.

"Every piece invites viewers to see themselves and their relationship to technology and waste in a new light," Silverman said. The exhibition runs through Sept. 10, 2026, with special programs including artist talks, salon discussions, and film screenings. Museum hours are Wednesday from noon to 5 p.m., Thursday and Friday from noon to 7 p.m., Saturday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 5 p.m. For event details, call 561-654-2220.

hero.headline: David Jolly selects Gwen Graham as running mate in Florida governor's race
hero.body:
Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly announced Wednesday at the state Capitol that former Congresswoman Gwen Graham will be his running mate for the 2026 election. Graham, whose father was late Florida Governor and U.S. Senator Bob Graham, brings a recognized name to the ticket. Jolly has positioned his campaign as a bipartisan effort to attract Democrats, independents, and Republicans who are unhappy with the current state government's direction.

Jolly, a former Republican congressman who previously served alongside Graham in Congress, emphasized that her background and experience were the primary reasons for selecting her rather than strategic political considerations. "I had one goal in this process: to identify a governing partner capable of leading this state, not just as lieutenant governor, but as governor," Jolly said. Graham outlined the ticket's priorities as affordability, education, health care, and insurance costs. She stressed that both candidates want to move beyond what she called divisive cultural battles and address an economy that does not work for everyone alongside problems in the education system.

However, the selection may face resistance within Democratic circles. Graham has long been associated with the party's establishment wing, and her potential involvement in the campaign had previously disappointed some progressives who sought greater diversity in the party's statewide candidates. Jolly responded to these concerns by asserting that the campaign remains committed to addressing disparities that affect communities of color. He further contended that Republican frontrunner Byron Donalds has failed to adequately address these issues. The Donalds campaign responded swiftly to the announcement, characterizing Jolly and Graham as failed politicians with a failed liberal agenda.

The announcement occurs amid ongoing conflict within the Republican primary. Former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lieutenant Jay Collins, and James Fishback have all requested a debate before the August primary. Donalds has countered that his Republican opponents are polling too low to warrant a debate and has called for Republican unity heading into the November general election. The dynamics of both races continue to develop as candidates prepare for the campaign season ahead.

cards.headline: DeSantis says Legislature diluted his property tax proposal, questions if amendment will pass
cards.teaser: Governor Ron DeSantis criticized the Legislature for changing his homestead exemption proposal and expressed concern about whether the modified measure will receive the 60% voter approval needed in November.
cards.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis said Wednesday in Brooksville that the Legislature substantially altered his property tax proposal, removing key components including a trust fund for fiscally-constrained counties. DeSantis stated the fund would have provided state grants to communities without the tax base of larger areas like Miami-Dade and to bedroom communities such as Pasco, Hernando, and Clay where residents commute elsewhere. He expressed concern that the modifications might prevent the constitutional amendment from passing with the required 60% voter approval in November. DeSantis said he will work with lawmakers in November and December to restore elements of his original proposal if voters approve the measure.

DeSantis also criticized the Legislature's decision not to apply the increased homestead exemption to school taxes, noting that school districts continue raising spending despite losing students. He pointed to Broward County School District, which doubled its budget to $2.5 billion over eight years while losing more than 50,000 students. DeSantis said districts avoid raising tax rates by increasing property values through appraisals instead. If approved by voters in November, the constitutional amendment would raise homestead exemptions to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, with further increases tied to the Consumer Price Index.

cards.headline: Pasco-Hernando State College receives $3 million grant for aviation program
cards.teaser: Governor Ron DeSantis announced a $3 million state grant for Pasco-Hernando State College to train aviation inspectors and mechanics at the Brooksville-Tampa Bay Regional Airport.
cards.body:
Pasco-Hernando State College received a $3 million Job Growth Grant to support its airframe and powerplant program at the Brooksville-Tampa Bay Regional Airport, Gov. Ron DeSantis announced Wednesday. The grant will help the college meet Florida's workforce needs in the aerospace industry, with about 100 students annually expected to complete the program. The funding will cover renovating and building specialized classrooms and labs, as well as tools and instructional technology. The program relocates the professional pilot program to the airport, placing aviation students alongside future mechanics to foster real-world training and strengthen the talent pipeline.

The $3 million comes from the Florida Job Growth Grant Fund, which supports economic development through infrastructure and workforce training across the state. The Legislature approved spending $40 million on the grant program in the 2026-27 state budget, though $20 million will be held in reserve until Jan. 5 for the next governor. School President Eric Hall said the college determined its needs by looking at what is happening in the region and emerging needs as Florida continues to invest in aircraft and aerospace innovations across the state.

cards.headline: Attorney General Uthmeier announces bust of illegal gambling ring in Southwest Florida
cards.teaser: Attorney General James Uthmeier announced the seizure of 479 illegal gambling machines and $294,000 in proceeds from operations in Collier and Lee counties, with 11 arrests.
cards.body:
Multiple law enforcement agencies joined forces to bring down an illegal gambling ring in Southwest Florida. Attorney General James Uthmeier along with officials from Lee and Collier sheriff's offices held a joint news conference Wednesday to detail the results of "Operation Sunset Stakes." The roundup netted 479 illegal gambling machines, $294,000 in illegal proceeds and arrests of 11 people operating the bogus gambling establishments. Uthmeier said illegal operations often connect with illicit money laundering, embezzlement, trafficking, large-scale drug sales and retail theft. The latest seizure brings Florida's confiscated gaming machines to about 3,114 so far this year associated with 81 arrests, approaching the record 6,700 machines seized in 2025.

Julie Brown, Chair of the Florida Gaming Control Commission, said operations like the Southwest Florida ring hurt many people. "When someone walks into an illegal casino, they don't have any guarantee of fair play. They don't have consumer protections. They don't have any recourse when they're being cheated," Brown said. During the news conference, Uthmeier announced his office sent cease-and-desist notices to payment processors including Visa, Mastercard and American Express who handle illegal online gambling transactions for sites including Bovada, BetNow and BetOnline. "If you're a payment processor and you're helping one of those sites, you are breaking the law," Uthmeier said.

cards.headline: Jacksonville CFO says city budget contains $275 million in excess spending
cards.teaser: Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia said Jacksonville's budget is bloated with $275 million in unnecessary spending, up from the $199 million in excess expenditures he previously identified.
cards.body:
Jacksonville's General Fund budget of $2.06 billion contains $275 million in excess spending, according to Florida's Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia. Ingoglia said the budget should have increased 41% since fiscal year 2019-20 to account for inflation, the Consumer Price Index, and population growth, plus a 5% buffer for large cities totaling $69 million. Instead, Jacksonville's budget increased 61%. He noted that Jacksonville's revenue would be $277 million lighter if a proposed property tax amendment passes, aligning with the $275 million spending overage he identified. Ingoglia accused Mayor Donna Deegan of using "scare tactics" to maintain the "bloated budget gravy train."

Mayor Deegan warned that a $300 million revenue hit from the amendment would force service cuts and result in road deterioration, library and park closures, increased public safety response times, worsening housing affordability, and more homelessness. She emphasized that current property tax revenue barely covers police and fire costs, which will increase as the city allows public safety employees to join the Florida Retirement System. Deegan argued the amendment amounts to a shell game benefiting some residents while impacting everyone, and that services outside the state's approved essential list, including libraries, parks, and housing programs, provide the greatest return on investment for the city.

cards.headline: Jeff Holcomb abandons House reelection to run for Hernando County Commission
cards.teaser: State Representative Jeff Holcomb is leaving his House District 53 reelection bid to run for Hernando County Commissioner, while current Commissioner Brian Hawkins will resign to run for Holcomb's House seat.
cards.body:
Jeff Holcomb is abandoning his reelection bid for Florida House District 53 to enter an already-crowded race for Hernando County Commissioner District 4. Meanwhile, current District 2 Commissioner Brian Hawkins announced he will resign from the Hernando County Commission to run for Holcomb's House seat, which covers western Hernando and northwest Pasco Counties. "After careful prayer, conversations with my family, and reflection on how I can best continue serving our community, I am announcing my resignation from the Hernando County Commission to pursue election to the Florida House of Representatives," Hawkins wrote in a statement Wednesday. A business owner and veteran, Hawkins has served on the County Commission as a Republican since 2022 and was up for re-election this year.

In the County Commission District 4 race, Holcomb joins incumbent Republican Board Chair Jerry Campbell, who is already fighting off challenges from Republicans Marvin Baynham and Jeremy Holmes. With Hawkins leaving the District 2 race, the remaining candidates include planning commission chair Kathryn Birren, "conservative conservationist" Maxwell Glenn and gun shop owner James Scavetta. In the heavily Republican 53rd District House race, Hawkins will face Democrat Tony Claude, an Air Force veteran, and Constitution Party candidate Christopher Anger. Holcomb, a Spring Hill Realtor and U.S. military veteran, was first elected to the state House in 2022 with 70% of the vote and won re-election in 2024 with 69% support. Primary Election Day is August 18.

cards.headline: Paul Renner claims he's winning with GOP base despite trailing in polls and fundraising
cards.teaser: Former House Speaker Paul Renner said he is winning among people actually paying attention in the Republican gubernatorial primary despite trailing Byron Donalds in fundraising and polls.
cards.body:
Paul Renner trails Byron Donalds in both fundraising and popular opinion polls, but the former House Speaker says the real story is being missed. During an interview with Liberty Sentinel, Renner argued that people who are actually paying attention in the GOP Primary electorate know he is the only choice to follow Ron DeSantis as governor. "Among the base level, the people that are actually paying attention, we're winning," Renner said. "We're winning in straw polls, not by a little bit, by a lot." The average of the 10 most recent polls dating back to last July shows Renner at 5% in fourth place behind Donalds, Lt. Jay Collins, and James Fishback.

Renner believes support for the frontrunner is soft and that his other two rivals are essentially the same as the Congressman from Naples. He drew a distinction between the political and donor class, which he characterized as transactional and seeking to back perceived winners, versus people wanting to preserve the Free State of Florida. Donalds has reported $81 million in fundraising through the end of May between his Friends of Byron Donalds political committee and his campaign account. Renner's latest fundraising reports have yet to be filed and are due by 11:59 p.m. Wednesday.

A Stuart woman has become an advocate after observing zero Florida Forever funds in recent budget discussions. She is raising concerns about the lack of funding for the state environmental land acquisition program.

Florida Forever has traditionally funded conservation and recreation land purchases across the state. The Stuart resident is working to draw attention to the funding shortfall.

The advocacy effort comes as state budget discussions continue. The Stuart woman is among those calling for restoration of Florida Forever funding.

cards.headline: Technician killed after vehicle falls off lift at Stuart auto shop
cards.teaser: A technician died Wednesday morning at an auto shop in Stuart after a vehicle fell off a lift.
cards.body:
A technician died Wednesday morning at an auto shop in Stuart after a vehicle fell off a lift. The incident occurred at a Stuart auto repair facility, according to reports.

Details about the specific location of the auto shop and the identity of the victim were not provided in initial reports. The incident happened Wednesday morning.

The circumstances surrounding how the vehicle fell from the lift remain under investigation. Auto lift accidents are rare but can be fatal when safety protocols are not followed or equipment malfunctions.

Authorities are investigating the workplace death. No information was available about whether other workers were present or injured during the incident.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man, 78, arrested for pointing gun at pregnant driver in road rage incident
cards.teaser: A 78-year-old Port St. Lucie man faces charges after allegedly pointing a loaded gun at a pregnant woman during a road rage incident Tuesday.
cards.body:
Robert Kniceley, 78, of Port St. Lucie was arrested Tuesday after police say he pointed a loaded gun at a pregnant driver during a road rage incident on St. Lucie West Boulevard. Kniceley was driving a yellow Chevrolet pickup truck east on the boulevard when he began honking and driving aggressively near the victim's vehicle. He pulled up alongside her vehicle at the intersection of SW Peacock Boulevard and SW St. Lucie West Boulevard, and when she rolled down her window, he allegedly pointed a handgun at her.

The victim is in the late stages of pregnancy and became scared for her safety, according to police. She provided video evidence of the man leaving the area. Police tracked Kniceley's license plate to his residence, where they recovered a loaded Smith & Wesson .22 caliber handgun with a round in the chamber. Kniceley was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon and transported to St. Lucie County Jail. A risk protection order seizure process was initiated as part of the investigation.

The Indian River Lagoon stretches along Florida's east coast, including portions of Indian River County. The three-and-a-half decades of data collection provides a comprehensive record of environmental changes in the estuary.
